explain.say: Rivers, wind and sea carry tiny bits of rock, called sediment, and drop them in lakes and seas. They settle in flat layers, one on top of another, year after year.

explain.say: As more layers pile on, their weight squeezes the lower ones and pushes out water. Minerals in the water act like glue, cementing the grains into solid rock.

explain.say: Different sediments make different rocks: sand makes sandstone, mud makes shale, and shells and skeletons of sea creatures make limestone. That is why cliffs often look striped.

explain.say: Unless the rocks have been flipped over, the bottom layer was laid down first and is the oldest. Geologists use this, and the fossils in each layer, to read Earth's history.

faq.a: Sand settles in layers on beaches, rivers or deserts, gets buried, and minerals like silica or calcite cement the grains together into sandstone.
Most limestone forms in warm, shallow seas from the shells and skeletons of sea creatures, which are made of calcium carbonate. They pile up on the sea floor and harden into rock.
Usually the bottom one. Layers pile up over time, so the lowest was laid down first. This idea is called the law of superposition.
asks: What is the law of superposition?

faq.q: Why do some rocks have stripes?
faq.a: The stripes are layers of sediment laid down at different times. Changes in what was being deposited, like sand, then mud, then shells, give layers of different colour and texture.

faq.q: Why are fossils found in sedimentary rock?
faq.a: Sediment gently buries dead plants and animals, which protects them. Igneous rock forms from melted rock and metamorphic rock is heated and squeezed, which usually destroys fossils.
asks: Why are fossils in sedimentary rock?

facts: Limestone is made mostly of calcium carbonate, often from shells and skeletons of sea creatures.
The Grand Canyon's walls show nearly 2 billion years of rock layers.

quiz.say: In a cliff of undisturbed rock layers, which layer is youngest?
quiz.why: Layers pile on top of each other over time, so the top one was laid down last.

wrong.1: The bottom layer was laid down first, so it is the oldest.
wrong.2: Thickness shows how much sediment piled up, not age.
